blocks.text: The module documentation defines numbering, storage-before-send, per-run locks, binding ownership, exclusive sequences, redelivery, terminal events, replayable types, and logging limits.
blocks.title: Emitter ordering contract

blocks.text: EmitterError subclasses describe missing bindings, ownership conflicts, and invalid events. Helpers reject non-replayable types, oversized/non-JSON payloads, invalid state transitions, and malformed replay lists before consuming sequence numbers.
blocks.title: Errors and pre-number validation

blocks.text: _Binding holds ownership, an ordering lock, and the highest sequence observed. _store allocates a sequence, builds an envelope, and appends it to replay in one worker-thread operation.
blocks.title: Per-run sequence state

blocks.text: ExclusiveRun exposes emit, state-change, terminal, and redelivery methods while its parent lock is held. Terminal emission advances the local tracker, unbinds, and sends live only.
blocks.title: Exclusive run handle

blocks.text: RunEmitter validates and establishes ownership, supports idempotent unbind and diagnostics, and yields an ExclusiveRun only while the current binding remains unchanged.
blocks.title: Binding and exclusive access

blocks.text: The public methods wrap the exclusive handle for normal events, state changes, terminal events, and replay. _send looks up the current connection and treats offline or closed peers as non-errors.
blocks.title: Public emission and delivery

gotchas: Offline delivery is normal because the event is already in replay.
Terminal events are not stored and are missed by offline devices.
A handle becomes invalid after its exclusive block ends.
how_it_works: Validates event types, payload sizes, state transitions, and replay lists
Binds each run to one user/device and lock
Numbers and stores events before sending them
Redelivers stored events or emits live-only terminal state
purpose: RunEmitter is the single sequencing boundary for run streams. It validates replayable event payloads before numbering, stores envelopes before attempting delivery, serializes each run with a lock, supports ordered redelivery, and emits terminal states from an in-process sequence tracker.
summary: Numbers, stores, serializes, and delivers replayable run events per device connection.
